title: Séquentiel organe défaillance évaluation (SOFA)-2 score
formula:
To calculate the SOFA-2 Score, add the points for each variables:

| Variable | Point | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Brain¹ , ² ( [GCS](nabda:calc.glasgow-coma-scale-score-gcs\) ) | 15 (or thumbs-up, fist, or peace sign) | 0 |
| 13-14 (or localizing to pain) ² or need for drugs to treat delirium ³ | 1 | |
| 9-12 (or withdrawal to pain) | 2 | |
| 6-8 (or flexion to pain) | 3 | |
| 3-5 (or extension to pain, no response to pain, generalized myoclonus) | 4 | |
| Respiratory ⁴ ( PaO₂ : FiO₂ ratio) | >300 mm Hg (>40 kPa) | 0 |
| ≤300 mm Hg (≤40 kPa) | 1 | |
| ≤225 mm Hg (≤30 kPa) | 2 | |
| ≤150 mm Hg (≤20 kPa) and advanced ventilatory support⁵ , ⁶ | 3 | |
| ≤75 mm Hg (≤10 kPa) and advanced ventilatory support⁵ , ⁶ or ECMO ⁷ | 4 | |
| Cardiovascular⁸ , ⁹ , ¹⁰ , ¹¹ | MAP ≥70 mm Hg, no vasopressor or inotrope use | 0 |
| MAP <70 mm Hg, no vasopressor or inotrope | 1 | |
| Low-dose vasopressor: (sum of norepinephrine and epinephrine ≤0.2 μg/kg/min) or any dose of other vasopressor or inotrope | 2 | |
| Medium-dose vasopressor (sum of norepinephrine and epinephrine >0.2 to ≤0.4 μg/kg/min) or low-dose vasopressor (sum norepinephrine and epinephrine ≤0.2 μg/kg/min) with any other vasopressor or inotrope | 3 | |
| High-dose vasopressor (sum of norepinephrine and epinephrine >0.4 μg/kg/min) or medium-dose vasopressor (sum of norepinephrine and epinephrine >0.2 to ≤0.4 μg/kg/min) with any other vasopressor or inotrope or mechanical support⁷ , ¹² | 4 | |
| Liver (total bilirubin) | ≤1.20 mg/dL (≤20.6 μmol/L) | 0 |
| ≤3.0 mg/dL (≤51.3 μmol/L) | 1 | |
| ≤6.0 mg/dL (≤102.6 μmol/L) | 2 | |
| ≤12.0 mg/dL (≤205 μmol/L) | 3 | |
| >12 mg/dL (>205 μmol/L) | 4 | |
| Kidney (creatinine) | ≤1.20 mg/dL (≤110 μmol/L) | 0 |
| ≤2.0 mg/dL (≤170 μmol/L) or urine output <0.5 mL/kg/h for 6-12 h | 1 | |
| ≤3.50 mg/dL (≤300 μmol/L) or urine output <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥12 h | 2 | |
| >3.50 mg/dL (>300 μmol/L) or urine output <0.3 mL/kg/h for ≥24 h or anuria (0 mL) for ≥12 h | 3 | |
| Receiving or fulfills criteria for RRT (includes chronic use) ¹³ , ¹⁴ , ¹⁵ | 4 | |
| Hemostasis (platelets) | >150 × 10 ³ /μL | 0 |
| ≤150 × 10 ³ /μL | 1 | |
| ≤100 × 10 ³ /μL | 2 | |
| ≤80 × 10 ³ /μL | 3 | |
| ≤50 × 10 ³ /μL | 4 | |

^1^For sedated patients, use the last GCS before sedation; if unknown, score 0.
^2^If full GCS cannot be assessed, use the best motor response score only.
^3^If the patient is receiving drug therapy for delirium, score 1 point even if GCS is 15. For relevant drugs, see the International Management of Pain, Agitation, and Delirium in Adult Patients in the ICU Guidelines.
^4^Use theSpO₂:FiO₂ratio only when PaO₂:FiO₂ratio is unavailable and SpO₂<98%. Cutoffs: 0 points, >300 mm Hg; 1 point, ≤300 mm Hg; 2 points, ≤250 mm Hg; 3 points, ≤200 mm Hg with ventilatory support; 4 points, ≤120 mm Hg with ventilatory support or ECMO.
^5^Advanced ventilatory support includesHFNC,CPAP,BiPAP, noninvasive or invasive mechanical ventilation, or long-term home ventilation. Scores of 3-4 require both an appropriate PaO₂:FiO₂or SpO₂:FiO₂ratio and advanced ventilatory support; ignore transient changes within 1 hour (e.g., after suctioning).
^6^Patients without advanced respiratory support can score at most 2 points unless ventilatory support is (1) unavailable or (2) limited by ceiling of treatment; if so, scored by PaO₂:FiO₂or SpO₂:FiO₂alone.
^7^If ECMO is used for respiratory failure, assign 4 points in the respiratory system (regardless of PaO₂:FiO₂) and do not score it in the cardiovascular system. If ECMO is used for cardiovascular indications, score it in both cardiovascular and respiratory systems.
^8^Count vasopressors only if given as a continuous IV infusion for ≥1 hour.
^9^Norepinephrine dosing should be expressed as the base: 1 mg norepinephrine base ≈ 2 mg norepinephrine bitartrate monohydrate ≈ 1.89 mg anhydrous bitartrate (hydrogen/acid/tartrate) ≈ 1.22 mg hydrochloride.
^10^If dopamine is used as a single vasopressor, use these cutoffs: 2 points, 20 μg/kg/min; 3 points, >20 to 40 μg/kg/min; 4 points, >40 μg/kg/min.
^11^When vasoactive drugs are unavailable or limited by ceiling oftreatment, use MAP cutoffs for scoring: 0 point, ≥70 mm Hg; 1 point, 60-69 mm Hg; 2 points, 50-59 mm Hg; 3 points, 40-49 mm Hg; 4 points, <40 mm Hg.
^12^Mechanical cardiovascular support includes venoarterial ECMO,IABP, LV assist device, microaxial flow pump.
^13^Excludes patients receiving RRT exclusively for nonrenal causes (e.g., toxin, bacterial toxin, or cytokine removal).
^14^For patients not receiving RRT (eg, ceiling of treatment, machine unavailability, or delayed start), score 4 points if they otherwise meet RRT criteria: creatinine >1.2 mg/dL (>110 μmol/L) or oliguria (<0.3 mL/kg/h) for >6 hours plus either serum potassium ≥6.0 mmol/L or metabolic acidosis (pH ≤7.20 and serum bicarbonate ≤12 mmol/L).
^15^For patients on intermittent RRT, score 4 points on days not receiving RRT until RRT use is terminated.

how_to_use.why: Quantifies organ dysfunction severity in critically ill adults, with better alignment to current practice than [SOFA](nabda:calc.sequential-organ-failure-assessment-sofa-score) .
how_to_use.when: Use in critically ill adults (≥18 years) in the intensive care unit (ICU).
how_to_use.pearls:
- Updated from the [original SOFA](nabda:calc.sequential-organ-failure-assessment-sofa-score) through a modified Delphi process and large, data-driven analyses to reflect contemporary organ support and thresholds.
- Developed using data from 1,319 ICUs across 9 countries (2014–2023), with internal and external validation in >3 million ICU admissions.
- On the first ICU day, SOFA-2 showed AUROC ≈0.79 for ICU mortality (vs 0.77 for SOFA).
- Not validated for use in pediatric patients or settings outside of the ICU (e.g., emergency department).
- Does not account for chronic causes of organ dysfunction.

next_steps.advice:
- Interpréter les résultats en parallèle d’une évaluation clinique complète.
- Des scores plus élevés traduisent une dysfonction organique plus importante et sont associés à un risque de mortalité en réanimation plus élevé.
- Le score aide à l’évaluation de la gravité et à la standardisation ; il ne s’agit pas d’un algorithme thérapeutique prescriptif ni d’un calculateur individualisé de mortalité.

before_use: SOFA-2 est récemment dérivé et nécessite une validation externe supplémentaire ; il n'a pas encore été intégré dans les principales recommandations de soins intensifs et ne doit pas remplacer les outils établis, tels que le [SOFA](nabda:calc.sequential-organ-failure-assessment-sofa-score) original.
